sections.title: Start white-label SEO reporting with the reader
sections.body: An executive reader needs the decision, priority and next owner. An implementation team needs URLs, evidence, dependencies and checks. Design the report for its audience without deleting the source record behind the summary.

sections.title: Audit more than the logo
sections.body: Check titles, file names, document properties, links, author labels, notification emails, shared spaces and meeting invitations. Agree whether the partner is invisible, named internally or allowed into a client-facing call.

sections.title: Separate activity from outcome
sections.body: Record what was researched or implemented separately from what changed in search or business data. State timeframe, source and limitations. Do not claim that a release caused a result when the evidence cannot isolate causation.

sections.title: Match reporting to decisions
sections.body: A status note can record blockers and approvals. A periodic review can connect released work with relevant signals. Reporting more often does not make evidence arrive sooner, so cadence should fit the decision cycle.

sections.title: Make every action assignable
sections.body: A client should know what the agency recommends, who approves it, who implements it and when it will be checked. Internal detail can be separate, but ownership should not be ambiguous.

sections.title: Keep an editable and stable record
sections.body: Provide editable material when the agency must adapt it, and preserve a stable source record for caveats and evidence. Review the final branded version before delivery so polish does not remove important conditions.
